[2] J. Henrard and A. Lemaitre. A second fundamental model for resonance. Celestial Mechanics, 30:197-218, (1983). doi: 10.1007/BF01234306

Estimating 3D human poses from single-view images is inherently ill-posed because of depth ambiguities and occlusions; however, most current approaches overlook these issues by predicting only one solution. In contrast, our method generates a diverse set of hypotheses that capture the full posterior distribution of feasible 3D poses. We achieve this through a normalizing flow-based approach that leverages the deterministic 3D-to-2D projection to address the ambiguous 2D-to-3D inverse problem. Furthermore, we incorporate 2D detector uncertainty to effectively model occlusions and uncertain detections. Key components of our success include a learned 3D pose prior and an extended version of the best-of-M loss. Our approach was evaluated on the Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP datasets, where it surpassed comparable methods across most metrics. The code is publicly available on GitHub.

Within numerical linear algebra, achieving nearly optimal bounds for tasks like rank computation, basis selection, regression, and low-rank approximation was previously thought to depend on resolving an open question posed by Nelson and Nguyen (FOCS, 2013) concerning logarithmic factors in the sketching dimensions of oblivious subspace embeddings. This study demonstrates that these logarithmic factors can be circumvented through a refined sketching approach, thereby yielding optimal or near-optimal results for the aforementioned problems. A central component of this method is an explicit mapping by Indyk, leveraging uncertainty principles and extractors; after applying standard oblivious subspace embeddings, this mapping efficiently disperses vector mass to make sampling highly effective. Consequently, the algorithm avoids the logarithmic overhead in sketching dimension typically incurred by bounds derived from the matrix Chernoff inequality. Specifically, for rank computation and basis finding, the proposed algorithms surpass those of Cheung, Kwok, and Lau (JACM, 2013), achieving optimality up to constant factors and a poly(log log n) term, respectively. Additionally, the paper introduces the first optimal algorithms for constant-factor regression and low-rank approximation, valid for the current matrix multiplication exponent.

Exclusive differential spectra arising from color-singlet processes at hadron colliders serve as high-precision benchmarks in both theory and experiment. This work introduces an effective-theory framework based on soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) to integrate massive (bottom) quark effects into resummed differential distributions. This approach accounts for both primary contributions from heavy-quark initiated hard scattering and secondary effects stemming from gluons splitting into heavy-quark pairs. Specifically, we examine the Drell-Yan process, focusing on the vector-boson transverse momentum ($q_T$) and beam thrust ($\mathcal T$) as representative exclusive observables. The theoretical formulation relies on the hierarchy among the hard scale, the quark mass, and the $q_T$ (or $\mathcal T$) scale, spanning from the decoupling limit ($q_T \ll m$) to the massless limit ($m \ll q_T$). The phenomenologically critical intermediate regime ($m \sim q_T$) necessitates the use of quark-mass dependent beam and soft functions. We compute all necessary components for describing both primary and secondary mass effects at NNLL$'$ resummation order—combining NNLL evolution with NNLO boundary conditions—for both $q_T$ and $\mathcal T$ across all relevant scales. For the $q_T$ distribution, we note that rapidity divergences differ from the massless scenario and discuss the characteristics of the resulting rapidity evolution. These findings enable a detailed analysis of quark-mass effects within the ratio of $W$ and $Z$ boson spectra at small $q_T$, a factor crucial for the precision determination of the $W$-boson mass at the LHC.

This paper introduces a novel reconstruction technique for real non-harmonic Fourier sums, defined as real signals expressible as sparse exponential sums of the form $f(t) = \sum_{j=1}^{K} \gamma_{j} \, \cos(2\pi a_{j} t + b_{j})$, where the frequency parameters $a_{j} \in {\mathbb R}$ (or $a_{j} \in {\mathrm i} {\mathbb R}$) are distinct. The approach leverages a recently developed stable iterative rational approximation algorithm \cite{NST18}. For signal recovery, we utilize a collection of classical Fourier coefficients of $f$ over a fixed interval $(0, P)$ with $P>0$. Although individual terms in $f$ may not be $P$-periodic, the proposed method necessitates at most $2K+2$ Fourier coefficients $c_{n}(f)$ to determine all parameters of $f$. We demonstrate that, given exact data, the iterative algorithm converges in no more than $K+1$ steps. Furthermore, if the number of terms $K$ is unknown and more than $2K+2$ Fourier coefficients ($L>2K+2$) are accessible, the algorithm can automatically identify $K$. Consequently, this method offers a robust new alternative to existing numerical techniques for recovering exponential sums, such as those relying on Prony's method.

Keywords: sparse exponential sums, non-harmonic Fourier sums, reconstruction of sparse non-periodic signals, rational approximation, AAA algorithm, barycentric representation, Fourier coefficients

The Galerkin difference (GD) basis consists of continuous, piecewise polynomials defined over a finite difference-like grid of degrees of freedom. These one-dimensional GD basis functions are extended to multiple dimensions via tensor product constructions applied to quadrilateral elements for the discretization of partial differential equations. This work introduces two strategies for managing complex geometries within a discontinuous Galerkin finite element framework using the GD basis: (1) employing non-conforming, curvilinear GD elements and (2) coupling affine GD elements with curvilinear simplicial elements. In both scenarios, the (semidiscrete) discontinuous Galerkin method remains provably energy stable despite variational crimes, and a weight-adjusted mass matrix is utilized to ensure that only the reference mass matrix requires inversion. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are established for handling metric terms in curvilinear, nonconforming GD elements to guarantee that the scheme is both constant-preserving and conservative. Numerical experiments validate the stability findings and illustrate the accuracy of the proposed coupled schemes.

It has been suggested that a hidden U(1) sector involving hidden photons might explain the Dark Matter present in the Universe. As these hidden photons traverse boundaries between materials with varying dielectric properties, they can transform into standard photons with wavelengths determined by the hidden photon mass. This contribution details measurements spanning the visible and near-UV spectrum, conducted using a large 14 m² spherical metallic mirror, and explores future dark-matter detection efforts in the eV and sub-eV ranges through the use of diverse electromagnetic radiation detectors.

Recognizing emotions in human users is a highly valued capability within Human-Robot Interaction (HRI). Nevertheless, current methods seldom leverage these detected emotional cues to actively adjust robot dialogue and decision-making for the user's advantage. This position paper introduces a method that integrates recognized emotions into a Reinforcement Learning (RL) dialogue management system, enabling it to adapt responses specifically to enhance the enjoyment of cognitive training tasks, such as the 2048 Puzzle Game.

This study examines the in-medium characteristics of hyperons and anti-hyperons using the Non-Linear Derivative (NLD) framework, with a specific focus on the momentum dependence of strangeness optical potentials. While the NLD model retains the simplicity of the established Relativistic Mean-Field (RMF) approximation, it introduces explicit momentum dependence at the field-theoretical level. The model's extension to the (anti)baryon octet follows SU(6) symmetry and G-parity principles. We demonstrate that, with suitable momentum cut-offs, the optical potentials for $\Lambda$, $\Sigma$, and $\Xi$ particles align with recent findings from chiral effective field theory and Lattice-QCD across a broad momentum range. Furthermore, we provide NLD-based predictions for the in-medium momentum dependence of $\overline{\Lambda}$, $\overline{\Sigma}$, and $\overline{\Xi}$ hyperons. These results are significant for upcoming experiments at facilities like CBM and PANDA at FAIR, as well as for applications in nuclear astrophysics.

Let $G$ be a connected, linear, reductive Lie group. We establish sufficient conditions for the well-definedness of the delocalized eta invariant $\eta_g (D_X)$, which corresponds to a Dirac operator $D_X$ on a cocompact $G$-proper manifold $X$ and the orbital integral $\tau_g$ derived from a semisimple element $g\in G$. We demonstrate that this invariant constitutes a boundary correction term in several index theorems that calculate the pairing between the index class and the 0-degree cyclic cocycle defined by $\tau_g$ on a $G$-proper manifold with boundary. Furthermore, we prove a higher-dimensional analogue of this theorem, addressing the pairing of the index class with higher cyclic cocycles defined by the higher orbital integral $\Phi^P_g$. This integral is associated with a cuspidal parabolic subgroup $P<G$, having the Langlands decomposition $P=MAN$ and a semisimple element $g\in M$. Finally, we apply these findings to define (higher) rho numbers linked to $G$-invariant positive scalar curvature metrics and $G$-equivariant homotopy equivalences.

The rapid expansion of Internet users in recent years has generated a vast volume of unstructured data, particularly within social media text. A significant portion of this demographic actively participates in health-focused networks to exchange medical information. This paper tackles a critical and timely issue by analyzing the sentiments and emotions users express regarding their specific medical conditions. To this end, we investigate users on prominent medical forums, such as Patient.info and dailystrength.org, focusing on discussions about asthma, allergies, depression, and anxiety. Initially, we establish a benchmark framework by crawling data and defining fine-grained sentiment categories related to medical conditions (Recovered, Exist, Deteriorate, and Other). We propose an effective architecture utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for data-driven feature extraction and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification. Furthermore, we introduce a sentiment feature specifically designed to be sensitive to medical contexts, demonstrating that combining this with CNN-extracted features enhances model performance. In addition to our custom dataset, we evaluate the approach on the "CLEF eHealth 2014" benchmark corpus, showing that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Learning directly from raw data, thereby reducing the reliance on manual feature engineering, is a key advantage of machine learning in numerous fields. Although many issues can be easily converted into vector formats for standard classifiers, other data sources naturally exist as structured interchange formats like JSON or XML (for instance, security logs). While current approaches, such as Hierarchical Multiple Instance Learning (HMIL), enable training on these raw structured inputs, interpreting classifiers built from such data has remained largely uninvestigated. By framing these models as subset selection problems, we show that interpretable explanations with desirable characteristics can be generated using computationally efficient algorithms. When compared to an explanation method adapted from graph neural networks, our approach achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in speed while delivering higher-quality interpretations.

This paper reviews recent developments in constructing cyclic cocycles within the Harish-Chandra Schwartz algebra of a connected real reductive Lie group $G$, and explores their implications for higher index theory concerning proper cocompact $G$-actions.

A new digital device has been created to evaluate the mechanical tension of wire arrays with defined length and density, alongside checking their electrical continuity and isolation. This instrument determines wire tension by detecting the fundamental frequency, operating by applying direct high voltage to adjacent wires and sweeping the frequency of an alternating high voltage across them. A resonance peak appears in the signal of the target wire when the alternating voltage's frequency matches its fundamental frequency. The system automates testing for up to 128 wires, reading eight at a time, and achieves a tension measurement accuracy of 1% using this digital wire analyzer (DWA).

We provide a comprehensive global study of the Higgs and electroweak sector within the SMEFT framework, incorporating a UV-completion based on a triplet extension of the electroweak gauge group. Utilizing functional methods, the matching is executed at one-loop order. In our SFitter analysis, we specifically address theoretical uncertainties stemming from this matching procedure. Our findings underscore the complementary nature of SMEFT and model-specific investigations.

We apply Bragg spectroscopy to a paraxial photon fluid. By employing wavefront shaping with a spatial light modulator, we imprint analogues of short Bragg pulses onto the photon fluid. Our measurements reveal the dispersion relation, confirming both a parabolic single-particle regime and a linear phonon regime, even under conditions of weak photon interactions and low sound velocity. Furthermore, we report the measurement of the static structure factor, $S(k)$, and demonstrate the existence of pair-correlated excitations, which indirectly indicate quantum depletion within the paraxial fluid of light.

When an amorphous solid undergoes homogeneous deformation, its response is characterized by heterogeneous plastic instabilities involving the localized, cooperative rearrangement of particle clusters. This heterogeneous behavior is crucial in determining the mechanical properties of such solids. In this study, we utilize computer simulations to investigate the characteristics and spatial correlations of these clusters, defined by non-affine displacements, within amorphous solids subjected to simple shear deformation under athermal quasistatic conditions. We observe that clusters with significant displacements are uniformly distributed throughout the material during the elastic regime but subsequently localize into a system-spanning shear band following yielding. The displacement field distributions display power-law characteristics with exponents that vary significantly with deformation. Furthermore, non-affine displacements exhibit strong spatial correlations that extend over longer ranges as strain increases. Our findings indicate that correlation function decay is exponential in the elastic regime, whereas the yielding transition is signaled by a sudden shift to a power-law decay. These results highlight the scale-free nature of non-affine correlations in the steady-flow regime and demonstrate that these findings are robust and independent of the specific strain window used to calculate the total non-affine displacement.

Pair-wise loss serves as a metric learning technique that generates semantic embeddings by optimizing a loss function designed to pull images from the same class closer together while pushing apart those from different classes. Although numerous variations of this strategy have emerged in the literature, this work decomposes the gradients of these loss functions into components that describe how they adjust the relative positions of anchor-positive and anchor-negative pairs. This decomposition unifies a broad array of existing pair-wise loss methods. Furthermore, explicitly constructing pair-wise gradient updates to isolate these effects provides insights into their relative impact and results in a straightforward algorithm that surpasses current state-of-the-art performance on the CAR, CUB, and Stanford Online Products datasets.

Few-shot learning is an emerging technique designed for scenarios with limited data, aiming to classify unseen categories using only a small number of examples. Recent methods, including metric learning, utilize meta-learning strategies that structure episodic tasks into support (training) and query (test) sets. These approaches show that simple models can perform well by learning a similarity function to compare support and query data. However, the feature space generated by specific metric learning methods might not fully leverage information unique to a particular few-shot task. This study investigates dimension reduction techniques to identify task-specific features that enhance prediction accuracy. We evaluate reduced features by scoring them based on intra-class and inter-class distances, selecting methods that maximize the separation between different classes while keeping instances of the same class close together. This module boosts accuracy by providing the metric learning similarity function with more discriminative features. Our approach surpasses metric learning baselines on the miniImageNet dataset, achieving an accuracy improvement of approximately 2%.

Single image-based crowd counting has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its diverse real-world applications. While numerous approaches utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been developed to tackle associated challenges, these models typically demand extensive training data. To address this, we present JHU-CROWD++, a large-scale, unconstrained dataset comprising 4,372 images with 1.51 million annotations. Unlike existing resources, our dataset captures a wide range of scenarios and environmental conditions, including images affected by weather degradations and illumination variations, thereby offering a rigorous benchmark. It features comprehensive annotations at both image and head levels. We evaluate several recent methods on this dataset, which is available for download at http://www.crowd-counting.com. Furthermore, we introduce a novel network, the Confidence Guided Deep Residual Counting Network (CG-DRCN), which progressively refines crowd density maps through residual error estimation. Built on a VGG16 backbone, the method utilizes the coarse density map from the final layer to iteratively generate finer predictions. This refinement process is guided by an uncertainty-based confidence weighting mechanism that filters for high-confidence residuals, ensuring effective learning. Evaluated on complex datasets, CG-DRCN demonstrates substantial reductions in counting errors.

Current methods for addressing dataset bias typically utilize a biased model to flag biased instances, subsequently reducing the influence of these instances during the training of the primary model to improve its robustness against out-of-distribution data. These approaches generally operate under the assumption that the primary model mirrors the biased model's behavior, relying on biases whenever possible. This paper demonstrates that such an assumption is not universally valid. Through a rigorous examination of two prominent datasets (MNLI and FEVER) and two biased instance detection strategies (partial-input and limited-capacity models), our experiments reveal that the biased model fails to accurately predict the primary model's behavior in approximately one-third to one-half of the cases. This discrepancy is evidenced by the significantly different input segments each model relies upon for decision-making. Furthermore, manual validation confirms that these findings align closely with human interpretation. Consequently, our results indicate that down-weighting instances identified by bias detection methods—a widely adopted practice—constitutes an inefficient loss of training data. We have made our code publicly available to support reproducibility and future research.

The application of right adjoints to the forgetful functors on $\lambda$-rings and bi-rings is utilized in the context of motivic measures and their associated zeta functions defined on the Grothendieck ring of $\mathbb{F}_1$-varieties, as conceptualized by Lorscheid and Lopez-Pena through torified schemes. This approach yields a particular subring of $\mathbb{W}(\mathbb{Z})$ that strictly encompasses Almkvist's ring $\mathbb{W}_0(\mathbb{Z})$, potentially serving as the ideal structure to house all local factors of completed zeta functions.
We investigate the counting function for rational points on conics, demonstrating that the threshold where asymptotic behavior emerges is determined by the magnitude of the smallest zero.

This study determines the Price of Stability (PoS) for First Price Auctions across all equilibrium concepts previously analyzed in the literature: Bayes Nash Equilibrium $\subsetneq$ Bayes Correlated Equilibrium $\subsetneq$ Bayes Coarse Correlated Equilibrium.
*   **Bayes Nash Equilibrium:** Under independent valuations, the tight PoS is $1 - 1/e^2 \approx 0.8647$, aligning with the corresponding Price of Anarchy (PoA) bound \cite{JL22}. For correlated valuations, the tight PoS is $1 - 1/e \approx 0.6321$, matching the corresponding PoA bound \cite{ST13,S14}. These findings suggest that, in worst-case scenarios, efficiency loss does not stem from variations in the selection of Bayes Nash Equilibria.
*   **Bayesian Coarse Correlated Equilibrium:** Regardless of whether valuations are independent or correlated, the tight PoS is consistently $1$ (100%), indicating no efficiency loss. This contrasts with the corresponding PoA bound of $1 - 1/e \approx 0.6321$ \cite{ST13,S14}. This result demonstrates that First Price Auctions can achieve full efficiency when broader equilibrium concepts are permitted.

We introduce a novel Dark Matter candidate termed Derivative Portal Dark Matter. This framework links the Dark Matter sector to the Standard Model via a massive mediator that interacts in a derivative manner. In momentum space, the derivative of this mediator aligns with the mediated momentum, which approaches zero in the limit of vanishing momentum transfer. Consequently, this model naturally accommodates Dark Matter relic density observations while evading tight constraints from direct detection experiments. Remarkably, the proposed framework also offers an explanation for the recently reported $W$ boson mass anomaly.

We explore magnon-photon interactions by utilizing a small magnet placed in an irregular resonant cavity, resulting in significant nonreciprocity with a high isolation ratio. Additionally, higher-order couplings between spin wave modes and polarized photon modes also demonstrate nonreciprocal behavior. These interactions between polarized photons and spin waves can be understood as an indirect multi-mode coupling between ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modes and spin wave magnons, mediated by cavity photons. We have derived a coupling matrix to forecast the characteristics of this indirect coupling mechanism. The presence of these indirect couplings expands the operational bandwidth for system nonreciprocity. Ultimately, the realization of nonreciprocal multi-mode magnon-photon coupling within a single system provides a viable approach to enhancing signal transmission quality.

This paper focuses on the mathematical investigation of nonlinear fractional Schrödinger equations featuring a general Hartree-type nonlinearity. We establish the existence and uniqueness of global solutions for the corresponding Cauchy problem. Furthermore, under appropriate conditions, we demonstrate the existence of standing waves via the concentration-compactness method by analyzing the related constrained minimization problem. Finally, we prove the orbital stability of these standing waves, which correspond to the minimizers of the associated variational problem.

Consider a compact Lie group $G$ of type $B_{n}$, exemplified by $SO(2n+1)$. This work characterizes the $L$-tuples $(x_{1},...,x_{L})$ of group elements $x_{j}\in G$ such that the product of their conjugacy classes possesses a non-empty interior. Equivalently, the convolution of the orbital measures supported on these conjugacy classes is absolutely continuous with respect to the Haar measure. This characterization relies on the dimensions of the largest eigenspaces associated with each $x_{j}$. Prior to this, such a result was established only for compact Lie groups of type $A_{n}$.

The weighted ancestor problem serves as a well-known extension of the predecessor problem to tree structures. While it is established that queries for this problem require $\Omega(\log\log n)$ time given $O(n\mathop{\mathrm{polylog}} n)$ space and weights within $[0..n]$ (where $n$ represents the number of nodes), applying it to suffix trees yields a surprising result: a solution exists with $O(n)$ space and constant query time, as demonstrated by Gawrychowski, Lewenstein, and Nicholson (Proc. ESA 2014). This specific variant can be restated as needing a data structure for a string $s$'s suffix tree that identifies any substring $s[p..q]$ in $O(1)$ time, effectively simulating a traversal from the root reading $s[p..q]$. However, the method proposed by Gawrychowski et al. lacks an efficient construction algorithm, which has restricted its practical application. This paper addresses that limitation by presenting a data structure for weighted ancestors in suffix trees that achieves constant query time alongside a linear-time construction algorithm. Our approach relies on a new technique utilizing irreducible LCP values.

This paper examines the behavior of particles within the spacetime of a non-rotating Konoplya and Zhidenko black hole situated in a uniform external magnetic field. The study focuses on circular trajectories for both electrically and magnetically charged particles, as well as particle acceleration. We begin by analyzing the motion of electrically charged particles, deriving expressions for the effective potential, energy, and angular momentum, accompanied by graphical representations. The investigation of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) reveals that its radius diminishes as the magnetic interaction parameter increases. Additionally, the dynamics of magnetically charged particles are explored.

Before the advent of deep learning, researchers in semantic parsing focused on understanding and modeling the various word alignments between natural language sentences and their meaning representations. The rise of sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models shifted this landscape by proposing that explicit alignments are unnecessary, as attention mechanisms can learn them automatically. However, recent scholars have begun to challenge this assumption. This study investigates the capability of seq2seq models to manage both simple and complex alignments. To do so, we enhanced the widely used Geo semantic parsing dataset with alignment annotations to create Geo-Aligned. We then evaluated standard seq2seq models on instances requiring monotonic versus non-monotonic alignments. Our empirical results indicate that model performance is substantially higher on monotonic alignments.

We investigate a broad category of multiplicative functions by connecting their "short averages" to their "long average." Specifically, we employ Fourier analysis and the enumeration of rational points on specific binary forms to asymptotically estimate the variance of these functions within short intervals. This approach yields significant advancements for various notable multiplicative functions, including $\mu_k(n)$, $\frac{\phi(n)}{n}$, $\frac{n}{\phi(n)}$, $\mu^2(n)\frac{\phi(n)}{n}$, $\sigma_{\alpha}(n)$, $(-1)^{\#\{p\,: \, p^k|n\}}$, and others, thereby generating new findings and refinements to existing literature on short intervals.

Under the assumption that the symmetric power $S^kE^*$ of the dual admits a Griffiths negative $L^2$-metric for some $k$, we establish the existence of a convex, strongly pseudoconvex, and Kobayashi positive Finsler metric on the vector bundle $E$. This proof utilizes the negativity of direct image bundles alongside the Minkowski inequality for norms. As a consequence, we demonstrate that any strongly pseudoconvex, Kobayashi positive Finsler metric can be enhanced to a convex Finsler metric retaining the same property. Additionally, we provide an extremal characterization of the Kobayashi curvature for Finsler metrics.

This research utilizes inexpensive, off-the-shelf radio frequency identification (RFID) tags as components for a reconfigurable surface. These battery-free tags are energized and managed by a software-defined radio (SDR) reader running adapted software, facilitating a source-destination link at a distinct carrier frequency. Theoretically, the study provides an optimal gain and the corresponding ideal element configuration, achieving tractable polynomial complexity rather than exponential complexity relative to the number of elements. Practically, it presents a specific methodology for designing and prototyping a wireless, batteryless, RF-powered reconfigurable surface, which is experimentally validated through a proof-of-concept. Additionally, the findings indicate that despite perfect channel estimation, the inherent weakness of backscattered links constrains performance improvements, even with a large number of surface elements, and the effects of channel estimation errors are also analyzed. Furthermore, future adaptations to various carrier frequencies can be easily implemented by making simple adjustments to the antenna and matching network of each RFID tag or surface element.

This study explores the potential for automating judgment in online one-on-one mathematics instruction. By constructing a Wide & Deep framework, we extract fine-grained predictive features from a small volume of noisy classroom dialogue to enhance student assessment accuracy. Experimental results on predicting students' mastery levels for sample questions confirm our model's superiority and practicality across multiple evaluation metrics.

This study examines quantum parameter estimation within an open quantum system utilizing both linear and Kerr-type nonlinear controls, treating the dissipation rate as an unknown parameter. We demonstrate that although these controls enhance estimation precision, they typically induce substantial deformation in the system state. Consequently, we introduce a multi-objective optimization framework to balance two competing goals: maximizing Fisher information to boost precision and minimizing state deformation to preserve fidelity. Furthermore, simulations of a simplified $\epsilon$-constrained model validate the effectiveness of Hamiltonian control in achieving improved precision for quantum parameter estimation.

This research examines toric nearly K\"ahler manifolds, building upon the contributions of Moroianu and Nagy. We provide a characterization of their global geometry through the use of multi-moment maps and subsequently explore both polynomial and radial solutions to the toric nearly K\"ahler equation.

It is widely recognized that access to vast amounts of training data is a critical driver behind recent breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Nevertheless, datasets are frequently constructed for specific tasks within narrow AI domains, lacking a standardized approach for management and access. This fragmentation not only introduces inefficiencies during the training and deployment of Machine Learning models but also hinders a deeper understanding of the data, which is essential for data-centric AI. This paper outlines our vision for a unified framework capable of integrating diverse datasets and enabling easy querying, for instance, through standard query languages. We illustrate this concept through our current development of a framework for Computer Vision datasets, highlighting its benefits across various scenarios. The demonstration can be accessed at https://vision.semkg.org.

We investigate the convergence of Krylov–Bogolyubov averaging applied to linear PDEs with a pure imaginary spectrum subjected to nonlinear stochastic perturbations. Our results demonstrate that when the resulting effective equation exhibits mixing properties, the convergence holds uniformly over time.

This paper presents an efficient technique for approximating matrix permanents through belief propagation. We define a probability distribution where the partition function corresponds precisely to the permanent, then apply Bethe free energy to estimate this function. Following the derivation of several optimizations for standard belief propagation, the final algorithm achieves $(n^2)$ time complexity per iteration. We conclude by illustrating the benefits of this approximation method.

Dowling previously demonstrated that the Whitney numbers of the first and second kinds obey relations analogous to those of Stirling numbers. More recently, Kim and Kim defined the degenerate $r$-Whitney numbers of the first and second kinds as degenerate extensions and further generalizations of these original Whitney numbers. It is well known that the normal ordering of an integer power of the number operator, expressed via boson operators, relies on Stirling numbers of the second kind. This paper observes that the normal ordering of a specific quantity involving the number operator can be represented using the degenerate $r$-Whitney numbers of the second kind. Consequently, we derive various properties, recurrence relations, orthogonality conditions, and identities for these numbers based on this normal ordering approach. Furthermore, we treat degenerate $r$-Dowling polynomials as a natural extension of the degenerate $r$-Whitney numbers of the second kind and examine their respective properties.

This study examines various methods for incorporating light-matter interactions into first-principles tight-binding (TB) models. While the velocity gauge, which relies on linear coupling to the vector potential, is the conventional approach for describing optical properties, finite systems permit a transformation to represent radiation via the electric field. This alternative, known as the dipole gauge, serves as a multi-orbital extension of Peierls' substitution, though complications emerge in periodic systems. We evaluate the accuracy and gauge invariance of both approaches within TB models derived from maximally localized Wannier functions. By focusing on representative two-dimensional materials, we develop these models and compute their electromagnetic responses under both linear response conditions and strong excitations. Benchmarking against fully converged first-principles calculations confirms the reliability of the TB approximations. Our results indicate that the dipole gauge consistently outperforms the velocity gauge in accuracy. The primary shortcoming of the velocity gauge lies in the incomplete cancellation of paramagnetic and diamagnetic currents. However, by formulating a corresponding sum rule, we can explicitly enforce this cancellation. This correction improves velocity gauge models, producing results that align excellently with the dipole gauge and restore gauge invariance.

Recent studies have shown that behavior signals gathered from smartphones and wearables can be used for long-term behavior modeling. However, a comprehensive public dataset serving as an open testbed for fair algorithmic comparison is currently missing. Furthermore, previous research has primarily evaluated algorithms using data from a single population over a short timeframe, failing to assess their cross-dataset generalizability. We introduce the first multi-year passive sensing datasets, comprising over 700 user-years and data from 497 unique individuals collected via mobile and wearable sensors, alongside a broad spectrum of well-being metrics. These datasets facilitate multiple cross-dataset evaluations to test the generalizability of behavior modeling algorithms across different users and time periods. As an initial step, we provide benchmark results for 18 algorithms on depression detection. Our findings suggest that while both existing depression detection methods and domain generalization techniques show promise, further research is required to achieve sufficient cross-dataset generalizability. We anticipate that these multi-year datasets will assist the machine learning community in developing generalizable algorithms for longitudinal behavior modeling.

We provide a theoretical investigation into the spatial configuration of two symmetric signals generated via degenerate four-wave mixing in a thin sample of two-level atoms using Gaussian beams. Our computations fully incorporate the spatial and spectral dependencies of the nonlinear susceptibilities governing these processes, uncovering two distinct phenomena. First, the total power of the incident beams influences the transverse profiles of the four-wave mixing signals both at the medium's exit and during their subsequent free propagation. Second, the spectral properties of the medium affect the longitudinal profiles of the generated signals as they propagate freely. We interpret the first phenomenon as medium saturation in high-intensity regions and the second as arising from a nonlinear contribution to the refractive index within the atomic medium. While these effects may exhibit symmetry between the two signals, asymmetries can emerge due to varying detunings of the incident fields from resonance.

Although the matrix element method is regarded as the premier inference tool for LHC analyses with limited event counts due to its high computational cost, we demonstrate that combining two conditional generative neural networks can model QCD radiation and detector effects without simplifying assumptions, enabling efficient likelihood calculations for single events. We apply this technique to determine the CP-violating phase of the top Yukawa coupling in associated Higgs and single-top production, noting that jet combinatorics currently remains the primary constraint on the method's precision.

We introduce MARINLINGA, a novel algorithm designed for reverse line graph computation, which involves reconstructing an original graph from its line graph. Unlike all prior methods that depend on Whitney's theorem, MARINLINGA utilizes a distinct and more straightforward approach based on link relabeling and endnode recognition. With a worst-case time complexity of O(N^2), where N represents the number of nodes in the line graph, our method proves to be more time-efficient than the well-established Roussopoulos's algorithm.

Although deep models trained via maximum likelihood have reached state-of-the-art performance in survival analysis, practitioners often assess them using alternative metrics like the Brier score (BS) and Bernoulli log likelihood (BLL) at specific time horizons. Since maximum likelihood does not directly optimize these criteria, such models may perform poorly on them. Directly optimizing BS necessitates inverse-weighting by the censoring distribution, yet estimating the censoring model itself requires inverse-weighting by the failure distribution. This creates a circular dependency where neither distribution is known. To address this, we propose Inverse-Weighted Survival Games. In this framework, each model's objective is constructed from re-weighted estimates involving the other model, which remains fixed during training. We demonstrate that if the loss is proper, the game always converges to a stationary point representing the true failure and censoring distributions, ensuring models do not deviate from these correct distributions once reached. We identify a scenario where this stationary point is unique. Furthermore, we show that these games effectively optimize BS in simulations and apply these principles to real-world data involving cancer patients and critically ill individuals.

We utilize archival data from Herschel, ALMA, and MUSE to examine the molecular ring of Messier 104 (the Sombrero galaxy), offering new insights into its interstellar medium. Our findings indicate that molecular hydrogen, traced by CO emission, and dust, detected via far-infrared radiation, are uniformly spread throughout the ring, whereas ionized gas, identified through H$\alpha$ and [CII] emission, appears in distinct knots. Although M104 is classified as an SAa galaxy, it exhibits characteristics common to early-type galaxies; consequently, we compared its [CII] and dust emission against a sample of early-type galaxies observed by Herschel and SOFIA. The [CII]/FIR ratio in M104 is significantly lower than that of typical star-forming galaxies but aligns closely with early-type galaxies. Optical emission line diagnostics reveal that regions identified as HII lie nearer to star-forming galaxies in the [CII]/FIR diagram than low-ionization regions. The strong correlation between [CII] and H$\alpha$ emission, combined with the absence of a correlation between CO emission and star formation, suggests that active star formation along the ring is minimal and that most [CII] emission originates from ionized and neutral atomic gas rather than molecular gas. Based on the total CO line intensity, we estimate the molecular hydrogen mass to be $0.9 \times 10^9 M_{\odot}$, a value falling between that of early-type galaxies and the molecular ring of our own galaxy.

Quantum Monte Carlo represents a highly effective numerical approach for investigating nonperturbative characteristics of quantum many-body systems. Nevertheless, its utility in real-time scenarios is constrained because the real-time evolution path-integral weight becomes complex and rapidly oscillating, which severely disrupts the sampling process. In this Letter, we demonstrate that certain real-time problems within open fermion systems can be addressed using Quantum Monte Carlo methods. We achieve this by establishing a correspondence between real-time dynamics in open quantum systems and statistical mechanics in non-Hermitian quantum systems; for specific instances, the latter avoids the complex measure issue. To illustrate this concept and validate its efficacy, we calculate the real-time evolution of fidelities in open fermion systems subject to dissipation.

We examine a specific class of holographic tensor networks that serve as efficiently contractible variational ansätze, function as explicit (approximate) quantum error correction codes, and are capable of supporting power-law correlation functions. Specifically, when the network comprises a single type of tensor that also acts as an erasure correction code, we demonstrate that it is impossible to simultaneously achieve local contractibility and sustain power-law correlations. Driven by this no-go theorem and the necessity of local contractibility for efficient variational ansätze, we offer guidelines for designing networks with multiple tensor types that can support power-law correlations. Furthermore, we present an explicit construction of such a network, which approximates the holographic HaPPY pentagon code in the limit where variational parameters approach zero.

This work addresses category-level perception, where the goal is to reconstruct the 3D pose and shape of an object from 2D or 3D sensor data despite variations within the same category (e.g., different car models). We employ an active shape model approach, utilizing a library of potential CAD models for a given category and estimating pose and shape through non-convex optimization based on 2D or 3D keypoints. Our primary contribution introduces PACE3D* and PACE2D*, the first certifiably optimal solvers for pose and shape estimation using 3D and 2D keypoints, respectively, both leveraging tight semidefinite relaxations. Second, we develop outlier-robust variants, PACE3D# and PACE2D#, supported by ROBIN, a general graph-theoretic framework for outlier pruning. This framework uses compatibility hypergraphs to model measurement compatibility; in category-level perception, these hypergraphs are constructed from 2D winding orders or 3D convex hulls, allowing many outliers to be removed via maximum hyperclique computation. Finally, we provide an extensive experimental evaluation, including ablation studies on simulated and PASCAL datasets. By integrating our solver with a deep keypoint detector, we demonstrate that PACE3D# surpasses the state of the art in vehicle pose estimation on the ApolloScape datasets while maintaining runtime suitable for practical applications.

For numerous practical applications, fully coupled three-dimensional models of lithium-ion pouch cells are computationally prohibitive. However, due to the small aspect ratio of typical pouch cell designs, these models can be effectively approximated by decoupling the problem into separate through-cell and transverse components. This paper integrates various simplifications for both through-cell and transverse models to construct a hierarchy of reduced-order representations for pouch cells. We provide a critical numerical comparison of these models under both isothermal and thermal conditions, alongside an evaluation of their performance using realistic drive cycle data. Finally, we offer recommendations for model selection that consider computational constraints and the specific quantities of interest for a given study.

**Introduction:** This retrospective study aimed to measure how the COVID-19 pandemic altered the timing of Emergency Medical Services (EMS) requests in Travis County, Austin, Texas, and to develop a reliable model for predicting pandemic-related EMS incidents. **Methods:** We examined EMS call patterns in the Austin-Travis County region from January 1, 2019, through December 31, 2020. Using change point detection, we identified key dates reflecting shifts in call distributions, and we utilized time series regression to forecast future COVID-19 EMS events. **Results:** Two pivotal dates highlighted the pandemic's impact on EMS call distributions: March 17, when non-pandemic daily incidents fell sharply, and May 13, when daily total calls recovered to 75% of pre-pandemic levels. The daily count of hospitalized COVID-19 patients emerged as a strong predictor of pandemic EMS calls, yielding an r² value of 0.85. Specifically, for every 2.5 COVID-19 patients transported by EMS, one patient was admitted. **Conclusion:** The average daily volume of non-pandemic EMS demand dropped significantly compared to the pre-pandemic era. Furthermore, the number of EMS calls for COVID-19 symptoms can be estimated based on daily new hospitalizations of COVID-19 patients. These results may benefit EMS agencies in planning for future pandemics by enhancing their ability to forecast related calls and tailor their responses accordingly.

The atmosphere and ocean interact closely, with atmospheric conditions driving ocean circulation and variability. However, the degree to which ocean processes influence the atmosphere over decadal timescales remains uncertain. Because low-frequency variability is hard to isolate from short observational records, climate models serve as the primary means to address this issue. This study evaluates how the ocean's intrinsic variability generates upper-ocean heat content patterns that fluctuate on decadal scales. These patterns may feedback into the atmosphere, influencing climate modes like El Niño and the Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation. We utilized output from a global ocean-sea ice circulation model at three horizontal resolutions, all driven by identical atmospheric reanalysis data. To separate the ocean's direct response to atmospheric forcing from its intrinsic dynamics, we compared simulations using inter-annually varying forcing (1958–2018) against those using repeat-year forcing. Coarse-resolution models relying on eddy parameterizations exhibited (i) significantly lower variance in decadal upper-ocean heat content and (ii) distinct spatial patterns of low-frequency variability compared to higher-resolution models. Since climate projections typically employ general circulation models with coarse ocean components, these biases impair our ability to forecast decadal climate modes and hinder overall climate projections. Consequently, our findings suggest that the scientific community should transition toward coupled climate models featuring higher oceanic resolution to improve future projections.

An isovariant map is defined as an equivariant mapping between $G$-spaces that strictly maintains isotropy groups. This work develops an isovariant counterpart to the Klein-Williams equivariant intersection theory for finite groups. We demonstrate that, provided specific dimension and codimension constraints are met for the fixed subspaces of $H$ (where $H\leq G$), the fixed points of a self-map on a compact $G$-manifold can be removed isovariantly precisely when the equivariant Reidemeister trace of the map is zero. To achieve this, we construct a novel Quillen model structure on the category of isovariant spaces, ensuring that $G$-manifolds are both fibrant and cofibrant, which results in an isovariant version of Whitehead's theorem. Furthermore, we explore the potential of isovariant homotopy theory in differentiating manifolds based on homeomorphism.

Environmental dynamics degrade camera localization accuracy by violating the static environment assumption inherent in SLAM algorithms. While recent approaches often combine semantic and geometric constraints to handle dynamic objects, they frequently suffer from issues like inadequate real-time performance, misclassification of people as rigid bodies, and suboptimal results in low-dynamic scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper introduces CFP-SLAM, a dynamic scene-oriented visual SLAM algorithm leveraging object detection and a coarse-to-fine static probability estimation. The method integrates semantic and geometric constraints to compute static probabilities for objects, keypoints, and map points, utilizing these values as weights in camera pose estimation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that CFP-SLAM achieves near-state-of-the-art performance across both high and low dynamic scenarios while maintaining high real-time capabilities.

Scaling Visual Question Answering (VQA) to accommodate the open-domain and multi-hop characteristics of web searches necessitates significant breakthroughs in visual representation learning, knowledge aggregation, and language generation. This paper presents WebQA, a demanding new benchmark that currently eludes large-scale state-of-the-art models—due to their inability to generate language-grounded visual representations for novel objects and limited reasoning capabilities—yet remains straightforward for humans. WebQA simulates human web usage by following three steps: asking a question, selecting sources to aggregate information, and generating a coherent language response; this is the expected behavior for IoT devices and digital assistants. Unlike existing approaches that assume models must excel at either visual or textual reasoning, WebQA incorporates a secondary text-only QA task to ensure that enhanced visual performance does not compromise language comprehension. We challenge the community to develop unified multimodal reasoning models capable of answering questions regardless of the source modality, thereby advancing the creation of digital assistants that can query both linguistic knowledge and the richer visual online world.

The study examines how shear bands interact with crystalline nanoprecipitates in Cu-Zr-based metallic glasses using high-resolution TEM and molecular dynamics simulations. Findings indicate three primary interaction modes: shear bands may dissolve precipitates, wrap around them, or become blocked, outcomes that depend on the precipitates' size and density. Additionally, when the crystalline phase exhibits low yield strength, slip transfer through the precipitate is observed. Integrating these computational and experimental insights, a qualitative mechanism map is developed to classify these processes based on the critical stress for dislocation nucleation, precipitate dimensions, and inter-precipitate spacing.

Fixation offers a promising, natural approach for human-computer interaction, specifically in interactive image segmentation. This paper addresses limitations in prior research regarding the scarcity of suitable datasets and the ambiguity inherent in fixation-based interactions by focusing on Personal Fixations-based Object Segmentation (PFOS). First, we introduce a novel PFOS dataset created by meticulously gathering pixel-level binary annotations from an existing fixation prediction dataset, a resource designed to significantly advance future research in this area. Subsequently, leveraging the unique characteristics of personal fixations, we propose a new Object Localization and Boundary Preservation (OLBP) network for segmenting gazed objects. The OLBP network employs an Object Localization Module (OLM) to interpret personal fixations and identify target objects, while a Boundary Preservation Module (BPM) incorporates extra boundary data to ensure the integrity of segmented objects. Furthermore, the OLBP architecture is structured using a combination of bottom-up and top-down processing with multi-level deep supervision. Comprehensive experiments on our new PFOS dataset demonstrate that the proposed OLBP network outperforms 17 state-of-the-art methods and validates the efficacy of both the OLM and BPM components. The PFOS dataset and the OLBP network are publicly available at https://github.com/MathLee/OLBPNet4PFOS.

This paper investigates how soccer players leverage spatial relationships to dominate field sections and advance the ball up the pitch through sequences of "safe configurations." These configurations represent team setups where the ball carrier maintains a series of open passing lanes interconnected by clear passing routes. A core tenet of our research is that an attacking team's forward progression is hardest to disrupt when it possesses multiple high-quality options at every instant. We offer empirical support for this claim. Our primary model is a directed weighted graph where nodes represent player formations, directed edges signify transitions between these formations, and weights reflect the frequency of such transitions. We conclude by outlining several applications and suggesting future research directions. We posit that our work provides a foundation for deeper exploration into safe ball advancement, strategy formulation, and advanced decision-making metrics. Specifically, we aim to streamline the process of advancing up the field for coaches and players by establishing a framework for generating novel, successful movement patterns and fostering new strategic approaches. Simultaneously, our study may help identify field configurations that frequently lead to turnovers or, conversely, offer significant strategic flexibility that hinders defensive containment.

*Because the contributions of the female authors to this paper were by no means less than those of the male authors, we have chosen to reverse convention and to list the authors in reverse alphabetical order to ensure that the female authors were not listed only after the male authors.*

The dynamics of many-particle systems are governed by correlations within their quantum states, making the analysis of these correlations the primary objective of many-body physics. Imposing any 'a priori' constraints on the relationship between global and local states—referred to as marginals—would significantly reduce the vast number of potential solutions for specific many-body problems, yet such constraints remain poorly understood. We establish an equality applicable to correlation-related quantities in any multipartite quantum system with finite-dimensional local components. This relation specifies a necessary condition for the consistency of marginal properties with those of the joint state. Although this equality applies to both pure and mixed states, the pure-state formulation, which relies solely on entanglement measures, constitutes a fully general monogamy relation for entanglement. These results hold significant implications regarding conservation laws for correlations and their connection to topology.

Music history big data encompasses information regarding time and user behavior, enabling researchers to accurately forecast popular song trends. While traditional prediction models excel at short-term forecasting compared to long-term, this paper introduces an improved LSTM Rolling Prediction Algorithm (LSTM-RPA). This approach integrates historical LSTM inputs with current predictions to inform subsequent forecasts, effectively transforming long-term trend prediction into a series of short-term tasks. Evaluation results indicate that the LSTM-RPA model achieved F-score improvements of 13.03%, 16.74%, 11.91%, and 18.52% over LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, and RNN, respectively. Furthermore, it outperformed traditional sequence models like ARIMA and SMA by 10.67% and 3.43% in F-score.
Code: https://github.com/maliaosaide/lstm-rpa

We utilize sequential deconfinement on a four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ $Usp(2N)$ gauge theory containing an antisymmetric tensor and $2F$ fundamental fields. This process yields a fully deconfined configuration represented as an $N$-length quiver. Leveraging this frame, we demonstrate the established self-duality of $Usp(2N)$ with an antisymmetric field and eight fundamentals. During this analysis, we identify a specific complication: in quivers featuring degenerate holomorphic operators, a straightforward application of Seiberg duality rules can result in an erroneous superpotential or chiral ring. Furthermore, we examine the reduction to three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories, where we recover known fully deconfined duals for $Usp(2N)$ and $U(N)$ gauge theories and derive new ones.

This study utilizes MeerKAT data to analyze magnetized radio filaments in the Galactic center, specifically examining the spacing within grouped structures. We present the morphology of 43 such groupings comprising 174 filaments. Unlike many straight filaments oriented perpendicular to the Galactic plane, numerous grouped filaments exhibit harp-like, fragmented cometary tail-like, or loop-like configurations. Notable instances include single filaments bifurcating into two prongs at junctions, suggesting plasma flow along the filaments. Observed spatial variations in spectral index, brightness, bending, and sharpening imply an evolutionary timescale of $10^{5-6}$ years. The mean separation between parallel filaments within a grouping peaks at approximately $16''$. Through modeling, we argue that filaments in a grouping reside on a common plane and that these groupings are isotropically oriented in three-dimensional space. Regarding origins, one hypothesis involves interaction with an obstacle, such as a compact radio source, prior to splitting and bending; in this scenario, the obstacle determines the filament separation scale. Alternatively, synchrotron cooling instability within cometary tails—formed by the interaction of cosmic-ray-driven Galactic center outflows with obstacles like stellar winds—could explain the phenomenon. This latter model predicts mean spacing and widths as a fraction of a parsec, aligning with the observed separations.

We aim to construct a confidence region for the parameters of a sample of size $N$ drawn from a Cauchy distribution. While this distribution involves two parameters—a location parameter $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ and a scale parameter $\sigma > 0$—we will estimate them simultaneously by treating them as a unified complex parameter defined as $\gamma := \mu + i\sigma$. The resulting region will be a domain within the complex plane, and we will provide a simple, explicit formula to represent it as either a disc or a square.

This paper offers a comprehensive analysis of the bottleneck within convolutional autoencoders (CAEs). As a critical component of modern deep learning, autoencoders and their convolutional counterparts are widely utilized by researchers and practitioners for diverse applications, including compression, outlier detection, and representation or transfer learning. Although CAEs are extensively used, our understanding of how bottleneck dimensions influence their emergent characteristics remains limited. Our findings indicate that expanding the height and width of the bottleneck significantly enhances generalization, thereby improving the efficacy of latent codes in subsequent transfer learning tasks. In contrast, the number of channels in the bottleneck holds secondary significance. Additionally, empirical results demonstrate that, contrary to common assumptions, CAEs do not merely replicate their input—even when the bottleneck contains as many neurons as there are pixels in the input image. This absence of copying persists even after training for 1,000 epochs on a small dataset of approximately 600 images. We contend that these insights are directly applicable and will facilitate advancements in models dependent on CAEs.

This exploratory qualitative study investigates how writers engage with next-phrase suggestions, addressing a gap in existing literature that has primarily focused on quantitative metrics rather than the nuanced interaction between writers and suggestion systems, particularly for non-native English speakers. In our study, amateur writers composed two movie reviews each—one without suggestions and one with—to observe their behavior. Our findings reveal that writers interact with these suggestions in complex ways; they can abstract and integrate multiple elements from a suggestion even when disagreeing with the suggestion as a whole. Furthermore, the suggestion system influenced various aspects of the writing process in unique manners. We propose a model of writer-suggestion interaction tailored for GPT-2 in the context of movie review generation, followed by recommendations for future research and design opportunities.

Since their discovery, the origins and mechanisms of fast radio bursts (FRBs)—short radio pulses originating from cosmological distances—have remained a significant mystery. We report the detection of a strong 40 Hz Quasi-Periodic Oscillation (QPO) in the X-ray burst from the magnetar SGR J1935+2154, which is associated with FRB 200428. This signal was significantly detected by the Hard X-ray Modulation Telescope (Insight-HXMT) and hinted at by Konus-Wind data. Given that QPOs from magnetar bursts are rarely observed, our 3.4 sigma detection (p-value of 2.9e-4) represents the strongest QPO signal identified from magnetars outside of extremely rare giant flares, rendering this X-ray burst unique. Furthermore, the two X-ray spikes coinciding with the FRB pulses align with the peaks of the QPO. Our findings suggest that at least some FRBs are linked to intense oscillation processes within neutron stars. Additionally, we demonstrate that if a QPO exists only for a fraction of the X-ray burst's time series, the Leahy-normalized periodogram may lead to an overestimation of the signal's significance and an underestimation of the QPO parameter errors.

**[Context]** While Requirements Engineering (RE) is a well-researched domain in conventional software development, creating Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems with opaque internal mechanisms presents unique RE challenges. Current literature predominantly examines using AI to facilitate RE, leaving a gap in research dedicated to RE specifically for AI (RE4AI). **[Objective]** This study examines existing methods for defining AI system requirements, catalogs available frameworks, methodologies, tools, and techniques for modeling these requirements, and identifies prevailing obstacles and constraints. **[Method]** A systematic mapping study was conducted to locate literature on RE4AI approaches. The analysis of 43 primary studies revealed the specific methodologies, models, tools, and techniques employed to specify and model requirements in practical settings. **[Results]** The study uncovered numerous limitations and challenges within current RE4AI practices. Findings indicate that existing RE applications lack sufficient adaptability for AI system development and underscore the necessity for new tools and techniques to support RE4AI. **[Conclusion]** Results demonstrate that empirical RE4AI research is heavily concentrated on autonomous vehicles and data management, indicating a need for further investigation into areas such as ethics, trust, and explainability.

The Vera C. Rubin Observatory will execute its Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) with a single-exposure depth of $r{\sim}24.7$ over an anticipated 10-year baseline. This approach enables deeper, longer-duration, and higher-cadence observations of the Milky Way's old halo compared to previous efforts like the PS1 3$\pi$ survey (Chambers et al. 2016), making LSST particularly well-suited for investigating variable star populations such as RR Lyrae stars (RRL). This work addresses the optimization of LSST's observing strategy, as the final survey footprint, single-visit exposure times, and repeat-visit cadences across various filters remain undetermined. We introduce metrics to evaluate how different observing strategies affect the reliable detection and classification of standard-candle variable stars. These metrics assess the ability to detect amplitude periods and phase modulation effects in RR Lyrae stars, known as the Blazhko effect (Blazhko 1907, Kollath et al. 2011), by analyzing simulated survey designs. Historically, the limited depth and cadence of typical all-sky surveys made studying this effect on large samples nearly impossible. Surveys with sparse observations over moderate baselines only permit fitting phase-folded RRL light curves, effectively integrating data over the entire survey duration and obscuring any period or phase modulation information. Conversely, surveys with sufficient cadence to detect subtle light curve variations often cover only small areas of the sky. In contrast, LSST's strategy will facilitate the study of variable stars in a manner that enables robust population analyses.

Since user preferences evolve over time, item reviews similarly mirror these shifting inclinations. Consequently, sequentially integrating review content into recommender systems necessitates the use of dynamical text models. This work utilizes the inherent value of reviews to improve rating predictions by (i) adhering to the causal sequence of review creation and (ii) establishing a bidirectional relationship where ratings inform language models and linguistic representations aid in rating prediction end-to-end. Furthermore, our representations capture time intervals, resulting in a continuous-time depiction of these dynamics. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach surpasses several state-of-the-art models, with source code available at [1].

We introduce CLIP-Lite, an information-efficient approach to visual representation learning that utilizes feature alignment with textual annotations. Unlike the original CLIP model, which typically requires multiple negative samples, CLIP-Lite optimizes its contrastive learning objective using only a single negative image-text pair for every positive one. This efficiency is achieved by leveraging an information-theoretic lower bound to maximize mutual information between the visual and textual modalities. Consequently, CLIP-Lite achieves superior performance despite being trained on significantly smaller datasets and batch sizes. We evaluated the model by pretraining on COCO-Captions and assessing its transferability to other benchmarks. Results demonstrate a +15.4% absolute increase in mAP on Pascal VOC classification and a +22.1% improvement in top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, outperforming or matching other complex text-supervised methods. Furthermore, CLIP-Lite excels in image and text retrieval, zero-shot classification, and visual grounding tasks. By explicitly aligning image and text representations, the method effectively harnesses language semantics to foster bias-free visual representations beneficial for downstream applications.

The thermochromic phase transition in Polycrystalline CuMo$_{1-x}$W$_x$O$_4$ solid solutions was investigated across varying compositions and temperatures using resonant X-ray emission spectroscopy (RXES) at the W L$_3$-edge, with findings supported by *ab initio* calculations. Analysis of the RXES plane yielded the crystal-field splitting parameter for 5d(W)-states, enabling the assessment of tungsten atomic coordination. Temperature-dependent RXES data successfully revealed the hysteretic structural phase transition between $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ phases during heating and cooling cycles, even at low tungsten concentrations ($x$<0.10). Results indicate that tungsten ions maintain octahedral coordination throughout the studied temperature range (90–420 K) for all samples, whereas in compositions with smaller tungsten content ($x$ $\le$ 0.15), coordination shifts from tetrahedral to octahedral upon cooling. However, for $x$<0.15, a fraction of tungsten ions remains in an octahedral environment at room temperature. These observations align well with the observed color changes in these solid solutions.

Training policies for robots to operate over long time horizons in intricate physical settings is crucial for applications like manipulation, yet achieving generalization to unseen tasks remains difficult. This work proposes attaining one-shot task generalization by separating plan generation from plan execution. Our approach addresses complex long-horizon problems through a three-stage process: constructing a paired abstract environment by simplifying geometry and physics, generating abstract trajectories, and solving the original task via an abstract-to-executable trajectory translator. By removing complex dynamics such as physical manipulation in the abstract environment, abstract trajectories become easier to generate. However, this creates a significant domain gap, as abstract trajectories lack low-level details and do not align frame-by-frame with executed trajectories. Drawing an analogy to language translation, our method employs a sequence-to-sequence model to bridge this gap between abstract and executable trajectories, allowing the low-level policy to adhere to the abstract plan. Experimental results across various unseen long-horizon tasks and different robot embodiments validate the method's effectiveness in achieving one-shot task generalization.

Superellipse sector particles (SeSPs) represent segments of superelliptical curves that define a flexible range of hard-particle geometries for use in granular and colloidal systems. These particles enable the continuous adjustment of corner sharpness, aspect ratio, and curvature, capable of modeling forms such as rods, circles, rectangles, and staples. The study evaluates three computational methods: pair-wise Monte Carlo simulations focusing solely on geometric constraints between two particles, extended Monte Carlo simulations analyzing these constraints across large particle dispersions, and Molecular Dynamics simulations facilitating interactions to generate random loose and close packings. The research examines how critical random loose and close packing fractions vary with particle parameters, revealing that both values generally rise with opening aperture and fall as corner sharpness increases. These observed packing fractions are contrasted with the Random Contact Model's mean-field predictions, showing discrepancies attributable to correlations in particle orientations. Furthermore, the intricate interplay between spatial proximity and orientational alignment is analyzed using a generalized Spatio-Orientational Distribution Area (SODA) plot. Results indicate that higher density packings emerge when particles adopt a limited set of preferred configurations, which are highly sensitive to both particle shape and system preparation methods.

This study introduces an asynchronous distributed leader-follower control strategy designed to implement Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) in three-phase unbalanced distribution systems by optimally managing smart inverters within distributed energy resources (DERs). A key aspect of this approach involves accounting for integrated primary-secondary distribution networks alongside voltage-dependent loads. To mitigate the computational burden caused by extensive secondary networks, the system is segmented into distributed leader-follower control zones according to network connectivity. Furthermore, to handle non-convexity arising from nonlinear power flow and load models, a feedback-based linear approximation utilizing instantaneous power and voltage measurements is developed. This facilitates the online execution of the method, allowing for rapid tracking of system variations driven by DERs. Additionally, the asynchronous nature of the leader-follower controllers ensures compatibility with non-uniform update rates and enhances robustness against communication delays and failures. The efficacy and reliability of this approach are verified through numerical simulations on a real distribution feeder located in the Midwest, USA.

Matrix computations have seen extensive application of the leverage concept, particularly leverage scores, which link matrix columns to subspaces defined by leading singular vectors. These scores assist in identifying column subsets capable of approximately factorizing a matrix with guaranteed quality, thereby underpinning numerous machine-learning techniques. This paper generalizes the definition of leverage scores to connect matrix columns with arbitrary subsets of singular vectors. By establishing a rigorous relationship between column and singular-vector subsets through the lens of principal angles between subspaces, we leverage this insight to develop approximation algorithms with provable guarantees for generalized column subset selection and sparse canonical correlation analysis. Numerical experiments further illuminate the proposed methods. The new bounds derived enhance our comprehension of fundamental matrix approximation concepts and offer foundational elements for future research contributions.

This paper introduces a Bregman framework that unifies several classical alternating minimization algorithms under a single mathematical formulation. We further provide a convergence analysis for this framework, demonstrating that stronger convergence results are achieved when the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property holds.

Although stochastic models are deemed more realistic for infectious disease modeling than the deterministic compartmental models typically employed, their application is hindered by estimation difficulties arising from missing data. This paper introduces a novel algorithm for estimating stochastic SIR/SEIR epidemic models within a Bayesian framework, a method that can be easily adapted for more complex stochastic compartmental systems. Leveraging the infinitesimal conditional independence inherent in the model, we derive a proposal distribution for a Metropolis algorithm that closely approximates the true posterior distribution. Consequently, unlike current benchmark Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms that update missing data points individually, our approach allows the proposal to cover the entire set of missing observations simultaneously. This enhancement dramatically improves MCMC efficiency, rendering stochastic models a practical option for disease modeling. The study provides the necessary mathematical theory and includes several real-world data illustrations to support these findings.

Maximum Entropy is a robust framework characterized by a clear distinction between relevant and irrelevant variables. Typically employed in inference after identifying relevant variables, it utilizes data to estimate a model capable of predicting dependent variables. Conversely, once a model is selected via Bayesian methods, Maximum Entropy can be used to directly extract the relevant variables (sufficient statistics) from the data. This study examines this approach within spin models featuring interactions of arbitrary order, detailing the inference of pertinent interactions. In this context, the dimensionality of the inference problem depends on the data's frequency distribution rather than the model's parameter count. The method's efficacy in recovering correct models across several prototype scenarios is demonstrated, along with its application to a real-world dataset.

This work tackles indoor scene generation by producing sequences of objects, including their positions and orientations, conditioned on room layouts. By leveraging large-scale datasets of user-designed interiors, we extract patterns to synthesize new scenes. Unlike existing approaches that depend on 2D or 3D visual appearances and explicit assumptions regarding object relationships, our method operates without appearance data, instead utilizing transformer self-attention to implicitly learn object relations. We demonstrate that this design enables faster scene generation while maintaining or enhancing realism compared to prior methods. Furthermore, the approach is highly flexible; it can be conditioned on both room layouts and textual room descriptions using only cross-attention mechanisms. User evaluations indicate that our generated scenes are preferred over state-of-the-art FastSynth results in 53.9% of bedroom cases and 56.7% of living room cases. Additionally, our method achieves an average generation time of 1.48 seconds, representing a 20% speed improvement over FastSynth.

We experimentally demonstrated, for the first time, a transverse magnetic (TM) mode laser within a photonic crystal (PhC) slab structure operating at room temperature. This research introduces a PhC nanobeam (NB) cavity designed to sustain a high-quality-factor (Q-factor) TM mode. To achieve a substantial and complete photonic bandgap, the PhC NB structures feature large air holes within a thick dielectric slab. Through numerical optimization, the PhC NB cavity was engineered to support a high-Q-factor TM mode exceeding 1,000,000 by quadratically reducing air hole radii from the center to the periphery of the nanobeam. A single TM mode lasing action was successfully observed at room temperature in an InGaAsP quantum-well (QW)-embedded, optimized PhC NB cavity using optical pulse pumping, with the QW layer undergoing light etching. We posit that TM mode lasers in PhC NB cavities incorporating lightly etched quantum wells are promising candidates for surface plasmon excitation sources or highly sensitive optical sensors.

Search engine query autocompletions accelerate the search process by suggesting full queries in a dropdown as users type. Typically, these suggestions rely on extensive logs of historical user input, which means that accidental or intentional misinformation can be incorporated into recommendations, potentially harming individuals, organizations, and communities.
